distinctness: Likelihood-aware independent or sequential importance proposals are distinct from prior-Sobol sampling and single-site Gibbs. No implementation, pilot, scan, or score is authorized or run.
mathematical_opportunity: For bounded peer vectors v_is and positive prior weights p_is, K(theta)=sum_i logsumexp_s(log p_is + theta dot v_is) is finite and differentiable; its gradient/covariance give exact tilted aggregate moments. Tilting within the retained support keeps coupled count/taxi/delay components intact.
exactness_contract: The original product prior times the unchanged exact t5 likelihood remains the target. All proposal densities and normalization factors must enter importance ratios; target Rao-Blackwellization must integrate its original support without silently tilting its prior.
t_objection: Student-t5 observation noise has no finite moment-generating function for nonzero real arguments. Do not apply a standard cumulant/saddlepoint construction to the combined t-noise aggregate. Tilt bounded peer priors only, or explicitly condition on the Gaussian precision-mixture variable while accounting for its density.
dependence_objection: A single product exponential tilt mainly changes aggregate location; it does not reproduce the likelihood-induced negative dependencies among compensating allocations. The independently audited worst cohort already had fairly close prior and observed aggregate means but importance ESS 3.53/16384, with one draw carrying49.8% mass. Mean centering alone is weak evidence for rescue.
stronger_variant: Sequential proposals based on partial aggregates and a saddlepoint approximation for the remaining bounded-peer sum could create dependence, with the unchanged t5 likelihood correcting all approximation error by exact importance ratios. The count coordinate is lattice/discrete and sums can have low-rank or multimodal support, so ordinary continuous-density approximations need explicit treatment.
risks: Convex-hull boundaries cause diverging tilt parameters; numerical clipping without accounting changes proposal probabilities.

Extremely small proposal mass on retained modes can make apparently high finite-sample ESS misleading. A defensive positive prior component and independent replicates would be necessary design choices, not evidence of adequate accuracy.
Per-draw/per-peer iterative saddlepoint solves can erase the speed advantage; no measured runtime exists.
Exact integration adds no new evidence and retains source/prior misspecification and local-factor limitations.
recommendation: Defer. A simple product mean-tilt is unlikely to address the demonstrated covariance/mode problem; a defensible conditional proposal would require a new fixed numerical design, exact tiny-state weights/enumeration checks, independent replicates and score-scale Monte Carlo error assessment before any source-only pilot.
